svg.aria-label: Azure credential model before the change: the customer's service principal secret is encrypted and stored by the platform, decrypted on every deployment and sent through GitHub Actions, so the platform holds standing access to the subscription.

g.text: Azure — credential model BEFORE
The customer hands over a client secret. Encryption protects it at rest, but the platform holds a key to their subscription for as long as the tenant exists.
CONTROL PLANE (platform)
GITHUB ACTIONS RUN
CUSTOMER AZURE SUBSCRIPTION
1 · ONBOARDING (ONCE PER TENANT)
the client secret is handed to the platform, and kept
Encrypt and store the credential
Form: subscription ID, tenant ID, client ID,
client secret, LLM key, Pinecone key
AES-256-GCM →
tenants.azure_client_secret_encrypted
Decryptable with the database and
PLATFORM_ENCRYPTION_KEY together.
Not involved
Onboarding runs inside the platform
itself. CI only enters at deploy time.
Service principal, created by the customer
App registration + client secret
Contributor at subscription scope
The secret expires after at most 24
months, and an expired one leaves the
tenant unusable until a script replaces it.
Nothing else exists yet — no Key Vault.
2 · EVERY DEPLOYMENT
Decrypt, then send it on
The platform decrypts the client secret
on every deploy, not only the first.
It travels as a workflow_dispatch input
alongside the LLM key, the Pinecone key
and the docs-signer secret.
Dispatch inputs are recorded in the run's
event payload, readable by repo members.
Four secret values in the run
Masked with ::add-mask:: as the
first step, so they stay out of logs.
azure/login with a creds JSON;
Terraform gets client_secret via
TF_VAR, not argv.
Masking hides them from the log,
not from the process.
Sign in, then terraform apply
Entra ID accepts the client secret and
issues a token for the subscription.
Resource group, ACR, Key Vault, storage,
Container App, docs-signer Function.
Terraform writes the app secrets into the
Key Vault it has just created.
3 · WHAT THE PLATFORM HOLDS
A standing credential to the customer's subscription
Stored: the Azure client secret, the LLM key, the Pinecone key and the docs-signer secret — all AES-256-GCM, all decryptable by the operator.
The client secret is the one that matters: it acts in the customer's cloud, at any time, without their knowledge and without a workflow run.
Weakness: whoever holds the database and the encryption key holds the customer's subscription. The customer's only protection is trust in the operator.
4 · REVOCATION AND BLAST RADIUS
Revocation
The customer deletes the secret in Entra ID, which
also breaks their own deployments until the
platform is given a replacement.
Rotation is a shared, recurring task, and the
24-month expiry makes it unavoidable.
If the platform database and key are taken
Every Azure tenant's subscription is reachable with
that customer's own Contributor rights, silently and
for as long as the secret remains valid.
A database compromise is therefore a cloud
compromise — the gap fig-23 closes.
Recorded as Known Limitation #2 in SECURITY.md before the change: the operator holds both halves, so every stored Azure credential is recoverable.
